drug_class: Central Nervous System Depressant / Antiseptic / Disinfectant
purpose: Medically, alcohol is used as a disinfectant and antiseptic to clean skin before injections or minor procedures. It is also found in some mouthwashes, hand sanitizers, and cough or cold preparations. In high concentrations, it can be used to treat certain types of poisoning under medical supervision.
how_it_works: When applied to skin, alcohol kills bacteria and germs by breaking down their outer coating. When swallowed and absorbed into the bloodstream, it slows down the brain and nervous system, which is why it affects judgment, coordination, and reaction time. It is broken down mostly by the liver, which can only process a small amount per hour.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness, dizziness, flushing, nausea, and headache are common. It can also cause dehydration, leading to that 'hangover' feeling. When used on skin, it may cause dryness or mild irritation.
warnings: Alcohol is highly addictive and can cause serious liver damage, brain damage, and heart problems with heavy or long-term use. It dangerously interacts with many medications including sleep aids, anxiety medications, blood thinners, and pain relievers. It should never be used during pregnancy, as it can cause serious harm to the unborn baby. Never drink and drive.
typical_dosing: For skin disinfection, apply a small amount to the area and let it dry before any procedure. As a beverage, medical guidelines suggest no more than 1 drink per day for women and 2 drinks per day for men — though many health organizations now recommend avoiding alcohol altogether for the best health outcomes.
